title: Alex Ovechkin after Capitals fans chant for one more year: ‘We’ll see’
content:
In what might have been Alex Ovechkin’s final home game with the Washington Capitals, he gave his thanks to the fans before getting drowned out by chants of “one more year” echoing around Capital One Arena.

“It’s great,” he said in an interview on the bench after being named the first star of the game against the Pittsburgh Penguins. “You guys support (me) through all my years. Obviously last night we had a big win in Pittsburgh, and tonight we needed your energy. Thank you so much for all your support. One game left, and it’s a big one.”

Every fan in attendance on Sunday received an Ovechkin-specific rally towel, special T-shirts were available for purchase and the intermission youth game featured players wearing yellow laces on their skates like Ovechkin.

In a nod to the potential historic nature of the game, Ovechkin took a pregame photo at center ice with longtime Penguins rivals Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang. Moments later, he and Crosby took the opening faceoff.

The Capitals won 3-0, with Ovechkin getting the primary assist on Connor McMichael’s empty-net goal with 2:44 left in the third period.

When asked his message to fans, Ovechkin said, “Thank you very much, guys. I love you so much. It’s been tremendous all year, so we’ll see what’s going to happen.”

His response to the next question, about facing Crosby in this game, was drowned out by fans chanting “One more year! One more year!”

Asked by reporters after the game about the chants, he said, “I will think about it.”

The NHL’s all-time leading goal scorer said earlier this month that he had yet to decide on whether he’d return for his 22nd NHL season. He declined to give a firm date, saying he’d share his plans for 2026-27 “in the summer.”

“I have to talk with Ted (Leonsis, team owner), with (general manager Chris Patrick), with Mac (president of hockey operations Brian MacLellan), and I have to make a decision in the summer,” Ovechkin said in an interview with team broadcaster John Walton, posted on X.

“Health-wise, I’m going to be 41 in September, so you just have to be smart about it,” Ovechkin said.

The team has maintained that the decision is Ovechkin’s to make, with head coach Spencer Carbery saying he’s “totally supportive” of the captain taking time to decide.

“We’re going to support (Ovechkin) and however he wanted to go out, he’s earned that right,” Carbery said in Toronto on April 8.

“We want to give him room as an organization to do what he wants to do. And we’re going to be supportive of it,” MacLellan told The Athletic in October. “What he’s done, the amount of respect we can give him, we’re gonna give it to him.”

Ovechkin has one regular-season game remaining on the five-year, $47.5 million contract he signed in 2021. He leads the team in goals with 32, hitting 30 goals on March 31 for an NHL-record 20th time in his career.

Washington is still mathematically in reach of a playoffs spot, sitting one point back of the Philadelphia Flyers for third place in the Metro Division, but can be eliminated if the Flyers win their game in hand on Monday against the Carolina Hurricanes.

The Capitals end their regular season Tuesday in Columbus.
